messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#7890 — metering-ingest-kafka-consumer-lag (group=metering-ingest-prod)

pagerduty: Alert details:
- symptom: consumer lag > 100k for multiple partitions
- trigger: backlog growth > 10m tokens in last 10m
- severity: P1 (potential invoice risk)

carla: acked. I'm oncall, starting triage. tagging @matt for consumer-side checks and @jordan for infra scaling options.

matt: ACK — running quick checks now.
matt: running: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --group metering-ingest-prod --describe`
matt: sample output: `TOPIC metering  PARTITION 0  CURRENT-OFFSET 12450000  LOG-END-OFFSET 12580000  LAG 130000`
matt: lag is concentrated on partitions 0,2,5. consumer replica count is 6, pod autoscaler shows 2 cpu throttles in the last 15m.

jordan: noted. infra shows a temporary pod scheduling delay on eu-west cluster, nodegroup scale events around ~15m ago. could be spot preemption churn.
jordan: recommendations — scale up ingest-consumer deployment to 12 replicas, bump resources for hot pods, and if lag doesn't come down, trigger consumer group rebalance by rolling restart.

carla: agreed. matt, jordan — please do the scale and then do a rolling restart of the metering-ingest consumers by partition affinity. keep restarts staged.

matt: scaling now: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment metering-ingest --replicas=12`
matt: increasing resource request on hot pods: `kubectl patch deployment metering-ingest -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"metering-ingest","resources": {"requests": {"cpu":"500m","memory":"1Gi"}}}]}}}}'`

matt: after scale: new pod count 12, starting warmup. re-checking lag...
matt: current lag: partition 0 LAG 68k, partition 2 LAG 54k, partition 5 LAG 61k. trending down but still high.

carla: good. initiate rolling restart on consumer pods in batches of 3 to force rebalance and allow catch-up. use `kubectl rollout restart deployment/metering-ingest -n prod --timeout=5m` but do in 3 waves.
matt: doing wave 1...
matt: wave1 done, lag drop: part0 22k, part2 18k, part5 25k.
matt: wave2 starting.

ops-bot: system: autoscaler added 3 nodes to eu-west-1-nodegroup-2 at 2026-03-14T18:07:12Z.

jordan: looks like node pressure cleared after scale. good sign.

sophia: @carla @matt — billing ops here. What's the customer impact? any chance token counts will be permanently wrong for invoices?

carla: quick summary for billing ops:
- risk: transient under-counting while backlog persists; it's a read/ingest delay not a dedup bug — no evidence of data loss so far.
- scope: approx 0.7% of ingestion partitions affected during the 00:30–01:10 UTC window; concentrated on EU-west ingestion frontends.
- immediate impact: invoice generation jobs that run while backlog exists may see lower token counts for high-throughput customers (>=500k tokens) — perceived under-reporting.
- recommendation: hold auto-invoice run for invoices scheduled in next 2 hours for EU-west customers and flag accounts with >200k tokens for manual review.

sophia: OK will pause invoice run and notify finance. can you provide an estimated recovery ETA?

carla: ETA: 60–90 minutes for lag to fully catch up after wave2 completes, but we'll monitor. if lag is still >10k after 90m we'll escalate to platform oncall to consider fallback routing to dedicated ingest nodes.

matt: wave2 done. final wave starting. current aggregate lag across group: ~18k and falling. per-partition per-second drain ~2.5k/s.
matt: logs from a consumer showing steady progress: ```[2026-03-14T18:15:12Z] consumer-7 partition=0 offset=12570000 end=12590000 processed=20000/s```

carla: good. applying mitigation checklist items in runbook (link: https://confluence.redwood/infr/runbooks/metering-ingest). I'm going to open an incident tracking ticket and change PD status to "acknowledged — in progress".

incident-bot: PD#7890 status updated: acknowledged by carla at 2391234580.

mike: taking secondary watch. i'll keep dashboard alerts and customer comms queue. handoff to @mike in 15m for monitoring/sla follow-up.

carla: handoff notes for mike:
- cause: transient node churn + CPU throttling causing consumer backlog
- actions taken: scale to 12 replicas, increased resource requests, 3-wave rolling restart
- current status: lag falling, aggregate ~8k at 2391234635, trending down; monitor for 2 hours; hold invoice runs in EU-west for 2h and flag high-volume accounts for manual review.

sophia: acknowledged — finance paused invoice run and will coordinate manual reviews if counts don't reconcile after catch-up. will open a follow-up if any customers report billing discrepancies.

carla: leaving a follow-up task to run a reconciliation job after catch-up: `python tools/reconcile_tokens.py --since 2026-03-14T00:00:00Z --region eu-west --threshold 0.1`

carla: closing pager but keeping incident open for monitoring. will update with reconciliation result. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PD#7890 auto-escalation suppressed; incident moved to monitoring state at 2391234635."
